input.quote: (b) IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED ONE HALF OF THE AMOUNT PAID BY THE LICENSEE TO Licensor HEREUNDER.
input.rationale: Article XIII caps only Licensor's liability, at one half of amounts paid — well below six months' fees — while Licensee's liability (including its broad Article XII indemnity) is entirely uncapped and no carve-outs exist. That is walk-away territory on both counts (one-sided cap; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside/outside asymmetry). We target the fallback: a mutual cap based on 12 months' fees with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct. We have not disturbed the one-sided consequential-damages exclusion in clause (a) or clause (c), which fall outside the fallback checklist but remain noted for negotiation.

proposal.summary: Make the liability cap mutual, set it at 12 months' fees, and place indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We made the cap mutual and aligned it to twelve months' fees instead of one half of all amounts paid, and we placed indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap. This is our fallback position on limitation of liability.

ops.oldText: (b) IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED ONE HALF OF THE AMOUNT PAID BY THE LICENSEE TO Licensor HEREUNDER.
ops.newText: (b) IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY THE LICENSEE TO Licensor HEREUNDER IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM.

ops.text: The limitation in clause (b) above shall not apply to a party's indemnification obligations, a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations, or a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

mappings.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
